input_messages.content: Hi there! I’m having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone. It’s been happening for the past few hours, and I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me figure out what’s going on?
Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.
Yes, I can follow your instructions and run any diagnostic actions you need. Please let me know what you’d like me to check first.
I ran the diagnostic, and it looks like my messaging app is currently unable to send MMS messages. What should I check next?

Here’s what I see in my status bar:
- I have some signal bars, but it says “Poor” and shows 2G.
- Mobile data is enabled.
- Airplane Mode is not on.

What should I do next?

I’ve changed my network mode to “4G/5G preferred,” and now my status bar shows excellent signal strength with 5G and data enabled. Should I try sending an MMS again now, or is there anything else you’d like me to check first?

I checked my APN settings, and here’s what I see:
- APN Name: internet
- MMSC URL: http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc

There don’t seem to be any errors or missing information. Should I go ahead and try sending an MMS now?
I tried sending an MMS again, but it still isn’t working—my messaging app still can’t send MMS messages. There’s no specific error message, it just won’t go through. What should I try next?
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned off on my device. What would you like me to try next?
I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it only has permission for “phone.” It doesn’t have storage or SMS permissions. What should I do to enable those?

I’ve granted both the storage and SMS permissions to my messaging app. I just checked, and now my app is able to send MMS messages! It looks like that fixed the issue.

Thank you for your help! Is there anything else I should do to make sure everything keeps working?
Thank you so much for your help and clear instructions! I’ll keep those settings as you suggested. I appreciate your patience and support—have a wonderful day!

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hi there! I’m having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone. It’s been happening for the past few hours, and I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me figure out what’s going on?

I can help you troubleshoot your MMS issue. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD format), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can begin assisting you.
Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.

Thank you for providing your information. To help you with your MMS issue, I’ll need you to perform a few quick checks on your phone. Are you able to run diagnostic actions on your device if I guide you through the steps? 

Let me know, and I’ll walk you through the first step to diagnose the problem.
Yes, I can follow your instructions and run any diagnostic actions you need. Please let me know what you’d like me to check first.

Great! Let’s start by checking if your phone is able to send MMS messages. Please run the can_send_mms diagnostic action on your device and let me know the result. 

This will help us determine if the issue is with your phone’s configuration or with your network/service.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I ran the diagnostic, and it looks like my messaging app is currently unable to send MMS messages. What should I check next?

Thank you for checking that. Next, let’s make sure your phone has both cellular service and mobile data enabled, as both are required for MMS to work.

Please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- If you see any signal bars (indicating cellular service)
- If you see a mobile data icon (like 4G, LTE, 5G, etc.)
- If Airplane Mode is on

You can do this by running the check_status_bar diagnostic action. Please share what you see in the results.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Here’s what I see in my status bar:
- I have some signal bars, but it says “Poor” and shows 2G.
- Mobile data is enabled.
- Airplane Mode is not on.

What should I do next?

Thank you for the details. MMS requires at least a 3G network connection—2G is generally not sufficient for sending or receiving MMS messages.

Please change your network mode preference to allow your phone to connect to 3G, 4G, or 5G networks. On your device, set the network mode to “4G/5G preferred” (or similar wording).

After you’ve changed the network mode, wait a moment for your phone to reconnect, and then try sending an MMS again. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you need further assistance.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I’ve changed my network mode to “4G/5G preferred,” and now my status bar shows excellent signal strength with 5G and data enabled. Should I try sending an MMS again now, or is there anything else you’d like me to check first?

That’s great progress! Before you try sending an MMS again, let’s check one more thing to ensure everything is set up correctly: your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for MMS to work.

Please run the check_apn_settings diagnostic action on your device and let me know if the APN and MMSC URL are set correctly, or if you see any errors or missing information. This will help us confirm that your phone is fully configured for MMS.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and here’s what I see:
- APN Name: internet
- MMSC URL: http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc

There don’t seem to be any errors or missing information. Should I go ahead and try sending an MMS now?

Yes, your APN and MMSC URL appear to be set correctly, and your phone now has excellent signal strength with 5G and data enabled. Please try sending an MMS message now.

If it still doesn’t work, let me know what happens (any error messages or behavior you notice), and we’ll continue troubleshooting if needed.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I tried sending an MMS again, but it still isn’t working—my messaging app still can’t send MMS messages. There’s no specific error message, it just won’t go through. What should I try next?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your network and APN settings look correct, let’s check if Wi-Fi Calling might be interfering with MMS. Sometimes, having Wi-Fi Calling enabled can cause issues with sending MMS.

Please run the check_wifi_calling_status diagnostic action on your device and let me know if Wi-Fi Calling is currently enabled.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned OFF.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned off on my device. What would you like me to try next?

Thank you for confirming that Wi-Fi Calling is off. Next, let’s check if your messaging app has the necessary permissions to send MMS, specifically storage and SMS permissions.

Please run the check_app_permissions diagnostic action for your messaging app and let me know if both “storage” and “sms” permissions are granted. If either is missing, let me know which one(s) so I can guide you on how to enable them.
The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser
App 'messaging' has permission for: phone.
I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it only has permission for “phone.” It doesn’t have storage or SMS permissions. What should I do to enable those?

To enable MMS functionality, your messaging app needs both “storage” and “sms” permissions. Please grant these permissions to your messaging app:

1. Grant the “storage” permission.
2. Grant the “sms” permission.

After granting both permissions, try sending an MMS again. Let me know if it works or if you encounter any issues.

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Success. Permission 'sms' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app can send MMS messages.

I’ve granted both the storage and SMS permissions to my messaging app. I just checked, and now my app is able to send MMS messages! It looks like that fixed the issue.

Thank you for your help! Is there anything else I should do to make sure everything keeps working?

I’m glad to hear that granting the necessary permissions resolved your MMS issue! There’s nothing else you need to do at this time. Just make sure your messaging app keeps those permissions enabled, and your network mode stays set to 4G/5G preferred for the best experience.

If you have any other issues or questions in the future, feel free to reach out. Have a great day!
